paper_metadata.title: Quantum optimisation via maximally amplified states

experiments.description: MAOA and RGAS evaluated on a 10-location capacitated vehicle routing problem, with success probability vs computational effort compared across several restricted rotation counts and against unrestricted GAS and classical random sampling.

algorithm.ansatz: Grover rotation + Grover diffusion on a complete graph with binary threshold marking
algorithm.optimizer: Nelder-Mead for threshold-finding subroutine; adaptive search for final threshold
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Threshold search proceeds until 20 consecutive successful measurements at a threshold; final adaptive search continues until 40 consecutive successful marked measurements
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial threshold set near sample median; threshold step size from sample quartiles; appendix optimization used random initial parameter sets

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One basis state per feasible route/solution; binary marking function marks solutions below a cost threshold; complete-graph mixer used for Grover-equivalent amplification
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Feasibility encoded in the solution space; threshold marking selects solutions with cost below T

problem_instance.description: Randomly generated 10-location capacitated vehicle routing problem

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical random sampling baseline; unrestricted GAS used as comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Precompute solution-quality distribution for the CVRP instance
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Select best sampled solution / compute success probability vs effort

results.unit: 2r+1 linear speedup; exact numeric speedup depends on r

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic amplification in marked-state probability: (2r+1)^2; speedup over classical random sampling: 2r+1
speedup_claims.conditions: for thresholds in the low-convergence regime; repeated preparation and measurement of the maximally amplified state; restricted circuit depth with r Grover rotations
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states this is the maximum possible within amplitude-amplification algorithms and assumes the threshold-finding subroutine succeeds.

speedup_claims.factor: maximum amplification of a single marked solution on a complete graph is 9 for one iteration
speedup_claims.conditions: binary marking on complete graph with gamma=pi and t=pi/N
speedup_claims.caveats: Derived from Eq. (6) in the low-convergence limit.

experiments.description: RGAS evaluated on the same 10-location capacitated vehicle routing problem as a restricted-depth version of Grover adaptive search, compared against MAOA, unrestricted GAS, and classical random sampling.

algorithm.ansatz: Grover search with adaptive thresholding and randomized rotation count
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Adaptive search with maximum allowable rotation count restriction; otherwise follows GAS-style improvement until target found
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Randomized rotation count drawn from a uniform distribution with growing upper bound controlled by lambda

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same CVRP solution-space encoding as MAOA experiment
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Feasible routes only; adaptive thresholding over cost

problem_instance.description: Randomly generated 10-location capacitated vehicle routing problem

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical random sampling baseline; unrestricted GAS used as comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Precompute solution-quality distribution for the CVRP instance
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Select best sampled solution / compute success probability vs effort

speedup_claims.factor: better than classical random sampling; worse than MAOA
speedup_claims.conditions: restricted circuit depth with r in {8,16,32,64,128}
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not provide a closed-form speedup factor for RGAS in this experiment.

experiments.description: MAOA and RGAS evaluated on a 20-asset portfolio optimization problem with a fixed net position and a two-threshold formulation (risk threshold then return threshold), compared against unrestricted GAS and classical random sampling.

algorithm.ansatz: Grover rotation + Grover diffusion on a complete graph with binary threshold marking
algorithm.optimizer: Nelder-Mead for threshold-finding subroutine; adaptive search for final threshold
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Threshold search proceeds until 20 consecutive successful measurements at a threshold; final adaptive search continues until 40 consecutive successful marked measurements
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial threshold set near sample median; threshold step size from sample quartiles; appendix optimization used random initial parameter sets

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio choices encoded as z_i in {-1,0,1} with net-position constraint; MAOA uses a binary threshold on risk then a threshold on return within the low-risk subset
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize expected return subject to low-risk constraint; return = sum_i R_i z_i, risk = sum_{i,j} sigma_ij z_i z_j
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Two-threshold approach: first fix risk threshold to lowest 10% of solutions, then optimize return threshold within that subset

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization over 20 ASX stocks with net position constraint I=7

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical random sampling baseline; unrestricted GAS used as comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute daily adjusted close prices, expected returns, covariance matrix, and precompute solution-quality distribution
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Evaluate success probability of finding the highest-return portfolio within the low-risk subset

speedup_claims.factor: MAOA outperforms RGAS and classical random sampling
speedup_claims.conditions: portfolio optimization with low-risk subset fixed to the lowest 10% of solutions
speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit numeric speedup factor is reported for this portfolio instance.

experiments.description: MAOA and RGAS evaluated on an arbitrarily large normally distributed synthetic optimization problem, with performance compared across target ratios and fixed rotation count r=64.

algorithm.ansatz: Grover rotation + Grover diffusion on a complete graph with binary threshold marking
algorithm.optimizer: Nelder-Mead for threshold-finding subroutine; adaptive search for final threshold
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Threshold search proceeds until 20 consecutive successful measurements at a threshold; final adaptive search continues until 40 consecutive successful marked measurements
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial threshold set near sample median; threshold step size from sample quartiles; appendix optimization used random initial parameter sets

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Synthetic continuous-quality solution space modeled by the standard normal distribution; marked set defined by a quality threshold T
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find solutions in the top target fraction of the quality distribution
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Binary threshold marking on quality; marked-solution ratio given by the normal CDF at T

problem_instance.description: Arbitrarily large synthetic problem with normally distributed solution qualities

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical random sampling baseline; unrestricted GAS used as comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Use standard normal CDF as the marked-solution ratio model
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute success probability vs computational effort

speedup_claims.conditions: large normally distributed problem; target ratio much smaller than final marked ratio; r = 64
speedup_claims.caveats: Derived in the large-problem limit from Eq. (18); assumes low-convergence regime and repeated measurement of the maximally amplified state.
